name_reason: Compliant fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>. 'chapter_event_handler' is the per-event dispatch-table family. '_4a' is the dispatch index 0x4A in the handler table @ 0x51B91 (entry @ 0x51CB9 = base + 0x4A*4; confirmed by xref From 00051cb9 [DATA]) -- a meaningful domain ID, NOT a Ghidra address residue (the function's own address is 0x35C32, unrelated to 0x4A; the whole file numbers handlers by table index). '__ch29_dyn_turn_event' accurately names the verified behavior (chapter-29 dynamic turn-event scheduler).
purpose: Chapter-29 per-event handler (dispatch idx 0x4A): drives an 8-stage rotating portrait cinematic, showing one chapter-portrait white-flash cutscene per call at fixed tile (0xA,0x1D) keyed on a stage counter, re-arming the next turn-event one player turn ahead until the final stage.
logic_summary: Reads stage = consumed_flags[0x10] (MOVZX, zero-extended). Calls fd2_cinematic_chapter_portrait_dump_with_white_flash(0xA, 0x1D, stage) to reveal the portrait for the current stage. If stage != 7 (not the final of stages 0..7), writes (uint8)(turn_counter + 1) into tile_event_data_table[+3] (hook entry 0's turn byte) to schedule the next dynamic turn-event one turn ahead; on stage 7 this scheduling is skipped so the rotation stops. Unconditionally increments consumed_flags[0x10] by 1 (8-bit INC) to advance the stage. In the binary the final advance+return is reached by JMP into the Class-3 shared tail @ 0x35992 hosted in fd2_chapter_event_handler_40 (MOV EAX,[consumed_flags_ptr]; INC byte [EAX+0x10]; RET); that tail-merge is a binary size optimisation and the inline increment in source is functionally exact.
